study: Schneider et al. 2021/2022, CESE project-based learning chemistry/physics
eval_evidence: CESE was developed by PIs Barbara Schneider & Joseph Krajcik (NSF grant to them); they authored this efficacy trial of their own program.
developer_evidence: Treatment teachers attended 3 in-person professional-learning days plus ongoing facilitator support; team members and experienced teacher facilitators (the project team) delivered and supported the PD.
cascade_evidence: Project facilitators/team members delivered the professional learning directly to treatment teachers; no train-the-trainer hop.
counterfactual_evidence: Control teachers received a 1-day NGSS workshop at the start of the year (an active alternative PD), though the report also confirms via exit surveys that control taught 'business as usual'.
coaching_evidence: Several times during the school year treatment teachers met in person with facilitators, who also connected via video conference / message boards / hotline; periodic facilitator support, not recurring in-class coaching cycles.
student_dose_evidence: Project-based learning changes the teacher's regular chemistry/physics instruction; no separate student tutoring, pull-out, or added instructional dose.
maturity_evidence: Efficacy trial delivered over one school year (2018-2019), with outcomes measured at end of intervention; course-length single-year delivery, no multi-year maturity axis.
